intended_object: One of the two open hyperbolic half-planes of the upper half-plane ℍ bounded by the oriented geodesic `geodesicLine g` (the image of the imaginary axis under g ∈ PSL(2,ℝ)). Specifically, it is the image under g of the canonical left side {Re z < 0}. This comes from the docstring and the module documentation.
explanation:
`geodesicLine g t` is `g • (i·e^t)`, so its image is `g • {Re z = 0}` (`range_geodesicLine`). The imaginary axis splits ℍ into the two open half-planes {Re z > 0} and {Re z < 0}. PSL(2,ℝ) acts on ℍ by isometries, so the g-images of these sides are exactly the two open half-planes bounded by the translated geodesic.

The definition `g • {z | z.re < 0}` is this image of the left side under g. The labels "left" and "right" depend on which g is chosen to represent the line. That matches the convention for an oriented geodesic, and the module documentation says so explicitly. The supporting lemmas fit the intended object: at g = 1 it is {Re z < 0}; for a translation by x it is {Re z < x}; it is open; it is disjoint from the line and from the right half-plane, and the three pieces cover ℍ; its frontier is the line.

The setting, ℍ with its PSL(2,ℝ) action, is the natural one for hyperbolic half-planes. I found no general version of this in Mathlib, so the definition is not too narrow.
